title: Prefix signature consolidation and slab defragmentation for prompt-caching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Reduce duplicated KV/prefix entries and GPU memory fragmentation while preserving low tail latency and improving batching efficiency. This ticket implements a two-stage prefix signature consolidation pipeline (fast sketch + exact canonicalization) coupled with GPU slab allocator defragmentation and a request-aware eviction policy so multiple requests that share semantically identical prefixes reuse the same KV fragments. Scope includes on-device representation changes, RPC compatibility layer, canary rollout, and dashboards for regression detection.
background: We observe repeated near-duplicate prefixes across independent requests (similar system/prompt scaffolding + small variable parts). This causes multiple KV-cache fragments with the same key material to occupy distinct GPU slabs because their serialization and internal metadata differ slightly. Existing work reduced naive duplication but left inefficiencies across shards and slabs. We need a consolidation approach that is safe for live traffic, minimizes CPU/GPU overhead, and cooperates with continuous batching and KV slice sharing.
approach: Design a compact 128-bit stable prefix signature generated deterministically from tokenized prefix + canonicalized metadata. Two-stage check: (1) fast 64-bit bloom/sketch to filter most non-matches; (2) exact canonical hash (128-bit) for final identity. Sketch implemented with SIMD-friendly ops on CPU and fallback on GPU for hot paths.

Store a canonical reference table mapping canonical signature -> KV fragment metadata (offset, length, slab id). Table kept in host memory with hot entries mirrored on device for O(1) lookup during decode/serve.

Modify slab allocator to support lightweight defragmentation: when a canonicalization collapses two fragments, mark the victim fragment for reclamation and update live pointer tables. Defragmentation performed incrementally during low-load windows and coordinated with batching so in-flight requests use an indirection layer (fragment id -> current slab location).

Eviction policy: request-aware LRU with coalescing. When two fragments share a canonical signature they share TTL/usage counters. Evictions trigger at fragment group granularity to avoid partial duplication.

Compatibility: add RPC version flag for legacy workers. If receiving worker lacks consolidation support, runtime falls back to per-request local keys. Rollout plan includes mixed-mode testing with traffic skewing.

Instrumentation: add metrics for canonicalization rate, false-positive/negative of sketch layer, memory reclaimed, average KV fragments per prefix, and end-to-end tail latency impact. Dashboards and alerts for any >5% regressed p95 latency or >2% increase in GPU memory per shard.

Benchmarks: target 18-30% GPU memory reduction for KV store on typical web-chat mix, 5-12% p95 latency improvement on consolidated workloads, and <2% CPU overhead for signature checks at 99th percentile throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalization pipeline implemented and unit-tested (sketch + exact).
Runtime lookup path uses canonical table with indirection; no correctness regressions on language output.
Canary on dedicated cluster shows >=15% KV memory reduction and no >5% p95 latency regression over 24h.
Eviction policy coalescing prevents re-duplication under synthetic replay tests.
Instrumentation present: dashboards show canonicalization_rate, sketch_fp_rate, fragments_per_prefix, reclaimed_bytes, slab_defrag_ops. Alerts created.
Migration/compatibility tests between old and new workers pass and documented in runbook.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: sketch false positives could incorrectly dedupe distinct prefixes -> Mitigation: exact 128-bit check before consolidation; audit logs for any exact-match dedupe event count.
Risk: defragmentation could race with in-flight KV reads -> Mitigation: indirection layer with CAS-style update; ephemeral pointer lifetimes extend until request completion.
Risk: additional CPU overhead on hot path hurts throughput -> Mitigation: microbench sketch using SIMD; adaptive sampling to bypass sketch for extremely hot prefixes after stabilization.
Risk: cross-version workers mis-handle canonical entries -> Mitigation: RPC version gating and compatibility mode that falls back to per-request keys for older workers.
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Ticket created after perf postmortem showed 22% KV memory waste on small chat workloads. Design doc linked.
2026-03-07: Prototype of 64-bit sketch + 128-bit canonical has unit tests; microbench shows 0.8us median overhead on CPU for signature computation.
2026-03-09: Ravi landed initial sketch library PR (github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/8123) - needs integration with request path. CI flakes observed on macOS SIMD path; investigating.

2026-03-10: Spike shows slab defrag approach can reclaim contiguous free ranges but requires small metadata increase (16 bytes per fragment) to track canonical group id. Trade-off: slightly larger metadata vs ~20% memory reclaimable.

2026-03-12: Meet with SRE and Perf to plan canary (clusters: dedicated-alpha-2, dedicated-beta-1). Agreed guardrails: enable for 5% traffic, monitor p95 and OOM events for 48h before increasing to 25%.
notes: Follow-up work: per-model signature tuning (some models benefit from per-token normalization), shard-level canonical snapshots for fast warm-start, and persistent canonical table backup to allow restart without rebuild.
Design decision log: chose 128-bit canonical hash (xxh3_128) vs full SHA family due to performance and collision properties in our sampling tests.
Open question: whether to store full normalized prefix text in host memory for debugging; storing increases host memory but simplifies post-mortem.
